# Generated CLI inventory

Every command path registered by the `triss` executable, with its arguments
and options. The semantic reference lives in [../cli-reference.md](../cli-reference.md);
this file is the machine-checked inventory.

## `triss init`

Add the triss delegation block to your project (or globally)

Options:

- `-g, --global` — install into the target agent global rules file instead of the current project
- `-t, --target <agent>` — target agent (claude | codex | both); omit for an interactive prompt
- `-f, --force` — force-replace an existing triss block without diffing
- `-s, --setup` — run the setup wizard before any rules write; preserve the selected init target and scope
- `--yes` — with --setup: non-interactive apply of a complete headless configuration (required outside a TTY)

## `triss ask`

Read a corpus and answer through the configured provider runtime

Options:

- `--provider <id>` — canonical provider id
- `-m, --model <id>` — <canonical-provider>/<native-id> selector, or a bare native id resolved against --provider or the effective default provider
- `--engine <id>` — execution engine (direct, opencode, opencode2, omp, or crush)
- `--protect-credentials` — Use the parent-owned credential proxy for the model projection.
A selected protected route fails closed — before any credential-bearing
spawn — when the raw key cannot be contained or the proxy cannot start;
there is no automatic downgrade to raw.
- `--no-protect-credentials` — override a persisted TRISS_PROTECT_CREDENTIALS=true choice for this run
- `-e, --effort <level>` — reasoning effort: low, medium, high, xhigh, or max
- `-p, --paths <paths...>` — files or globs to read
- `-u, --urls <urls...>` — http(s) URLs to fetch and convert to markdown
- `--stdin` — read piped stdin as an additional source (for `cmd | triss ask --stdin ...`)
- `-q, --question <text>` — question to answer about the corpus
- `--max-tokens <n>` — token budget for reasoning + answer
- `--system <text>` — override the system prompt
- `--format <format>` — response format: text (default) or evidence
- `--stream` — force streaming even when stdout is not a TTY
- `--no-stream` — disable streaming output (default streams when stdout is a TTY)

## `triss exec`

Route a task deterministically to ask, review, coder run, or chat

Arguments:

- `[task]`

Options:

- `--explain` — print the JSON route decision without executing anything
- `--pr <number>` — explicitly route to review a GitHub PR
- `--base <branch>` — explicitly route to review against a base branch
- `--review` — explicitly route to review
- `--skip-issue` — forward review linked-ticket lookup suppression
- `--paths <path>` — explicitly route to ask with a file path; repeat for multiple paths
- `--urls <url>` — explicitly route to ask with a URL; repeat for multiple URLs
- `--code` — explicitly route to coder run
- `--chat` — explicitly route to chat
- `--stdin` — let the selected downstream command read piped input
- `--provider <name>` — forward the inference provider
- `-m, --model <name>` — forward the model
- `-e, --effort <level>` — forward reasoning effort
- `--max-tokens <n>` — forward the token budget
- `--format <format>` — forward ask/review response format: text or evidence
- `--system <text>` — forward the system prompt to ask/chat
- `--stream` — forward streaming preference
- `--no-stream` — disable forwarded streaming
- `--engine <name>` — forward model execution engine
- `--agent <name>` — forward coder agent template
- `--session <id>` — forward coder session
- `--continue` — continue the most recent coder session
- `--isolate` — forward coder isolation
- `--no-isolate` — disable coder isolation
- `--allow-best-effort-caller-worktree` — forward coder isolation downgrade
- `--protect-credentials` — forward protected credential mode for model-backed and coder routes
- `--no-protect-credentials` — override a persisted TRISS_PROTECT_CREDENTIALS=true choice for this run
- `--restrict` — forward coder restriction
- `--no-restrict` — disable coder restriction
- `--cwd <path>` — forward coder working directory
- `--timeout <sec>` — forward coder timeout

## `triss commit-msg`

Generate a Git commit message from staged changes

Options:

- `--provider <id>` — canonical provider id
- `-m, --model <id>` — <canonical-provider>/<native-id> selector, or a bare native id resolved against --provider or the effective default provider
- `--engine <id>` — execution engine (direct, opencode, opencode2, omp, or crush)
- `--protect-credentials` — Use the parent-owned credential proxy for the model projection.
A selected protected route fails closed — before any credential-bearing
spawn — when the raw key cannot be contained or the proxy cannot start;
there is no automatic downgrade to raw.
- `--no-protect-credentials` — override a persisted TRISS_PROTECT_CREDENTIALS=true choice for this run
- `-e, --effort <level>` — reasoning effort: low, medium, high, xhigh, or max
- `--apply` — run `git commit -m <generated>` immediately instead of printing
- `--no-conventional` — use a free-form commit subject instead of Conventional Commits
- `--type <type>` — force the conventional type (feat | fix | refactor | …)
- `--scope <scope>` — force the conventional scope
- `--max-tokens <n>` — token budget (default 2048)

## `triss review`

Review a local change or GitHub PR through the configured provider runtime

Arguments:

- `[pr]`

Options:

- `--provider <id>` — canonical provider id
- `-m, --model <id>` — <canonical-provider>/<native-id> selector, or a bare native id resolved against --provider or the effective default provider
- `--engine <id>` — execution engine (direct, opencode, opencode2, omp, or crush)
- `--protect-credentials` — Use the parent-owned credential proxy for the model projection.
A selected protected route fails closed — before any credential-bearing
spawn — when the raw key cannot be contained or the proxy cannot start;
there is no automatic downgrade to raw.
- `--no-protect-credentials` — override a persisted TRISS_PROTECT_CREDENTIALS=true choice for this run
- `-e, --effort <level>` — reasoning effort: low, medium, high, xhigh, or max
- `-b, --base <branch>` — compare against this branch (default: auto-detect origin/HEAD or main/master/develop)
- `--skip-issue` — don't try to look up a Jira/Linear ticket from the branch/PR title
- `--stdin` — read an explicitly piped UTF-8 diff instead of Git or PR sources
- `--files <paths...>` — literal path selectors: review ONLY these files (repeatable; renames select both sides)
- `--issue <key>` — explicit linked-issue key (e.g. PROJ-123); PR prose never triggers tracker access
- `-q, --question <text>` — override the default review question
- `--max-tokens <n>` — token budget for the review (default 8192)
- `--format <format>` — response format: text (default) or evidence
- `--stream` — force streaming even when stdout is not a TTY
- `--no-stream` — disable streaming output (default streams when stdout is a TTY)
- `--payload-mode <mode>` — review payload mode: single (default) or shard (sequential whole-file shards; no global verdict)

## `triss usage`

Cumulative cost / token usage summary across all triss calls

Options:

- `--since <period>` — period like 24h, 7d, 4w (default 24h)
- `--month` — shortcut for --since 30d
- `--by-project` — break down by working directory
- `--by-model` — break down by model name
- `--by-label` — break down by call source (ask, review, chat, …)
- `--json` — dump raw log records as JSON
- `--reset` — clear the usage log (cannot be undone)

Show current configuration: API key, models, .env sources

## `triss migrate`

Migrate pre-0.42 Triss-owned configuration to canonical provider schema 2

Options:

- `--json` — emit one machine-readable migration result

## `triss update`

Check for a newer stable release; explicitly update standalone installs

Options:

- `--json` — emit one machine-readable status object
- `--apply` — apply the newer release to a validated standalone install
- `--rollback` — switch to the previous verified standalone version
- `--yes` — skip apply/rollback confirmation in non-interactive use
- `--break-lock` — separately authorize breaking a proven-stale update lock

## `triss config`

Manage credentials in ~/.config/triss/.env (global) or ./.triss.env (project)

## `triss config wizard`

Interactive setup (Easy by default, Advanced by choice). Optional target: a canonical provider id, coder, or an integration name (jira | linear | …)

Arguments:

- `[target]`

Options:

- `-g, --global` — save to ~/.config/triss/.env (default if not asked)
- `-l, --local` — save to ./.triss.env (project-local override)
- `-f, --force` — re-prompt for values that are already set
- `--standard` — explicit Easy path (same as the default interactive flow)
- `--advanced` — full Advanced wizard — providers, execution, connections, integrations, runtime
- `--yes` — non-interactive apply of a complete configuration assembled from existing files, the environment, and explicit flags
- `--agent <agent>` — headless host intent: claude | codex | both | none (non-TTY default: none)
- `--install` — allow installing missing engines in a headless run (without it, missing dependencies are reported)
- `--coder-engine <name>` — coder target only: coding engine to configure (opencode default, opencode2 beta, crush, or omp — see docs/engines/omp.md). `coder init` uses --engine
- `--coder-provider <name>` — coder target only: canonical provider id. `coder init` uses --provider
- `--coder-protect-credentials` — coder target only: configure the parent-owned credential proxy mode instead of the default best_effort_raw. `coder init` uses --protect-credentials
- `--coder-no-protect-credentials` — coder target only: persist/forward an explicit unprotected choice that overrides TRISS_PROTECT_CREDENTIALS=true

## `triss config set`

Options:

- `-l, --local` — save to project env file (./.triss.env)

## `triss coder`

Run a coding agent through OpenCode V1, OpenCode 2 beta, Crush, or OMP

## `triss coder init`

Install/configure a coding engine (opencode default, opencode2 beta, crush, or omp), provider key, permission policy, and agent templates

Options:

- `-g, --global` — save to the global scope (~/.config/triss/.env, ~/.config/opencode/)
- `-l, --local` — save to the project scope (./.triss.env, ./opencode.json)
- `--engine <name>` — coding engine to configure: opencode (default), opencode2 (beta — shares the opencode.json config; see docs/engines/opencode2.md), crush, or omp (see docs/engines/omp.md)
- `--provider <name>` — canonical model provider id
- `--protect-credentials` — Use the parent-owned credential proxy and strict executable-surface gates.
A selected protected route fails closed — before any credential-bearing
spawn — when the raw key cannot be contained or the proxy cannot start;
there is no automatic downgrade to raw. An explicit --no-protect-credentials
overrides a persisted TRISS_*_PROTECT_CREDENTIALS=true choice for this run.
- `--no-protect-credentials` — override a persisted TRISS_PROTECT_CREDENTIALS=true choice for this setup/run

## `triss coder run`

Spawn a coding agent through the configured provider runtime and print a JSON envelope to stdout

Arguments:

- `[prompt]`

Options:

- `--engine <name>` — coding engine: opencode (default), opencode2 (beta — see docs/engines/opencode2.md), crush, or omp (see docs/engines/omp.md)
- `-e, --effort <level>` — reasoning effort: low, medium, high, xhigh, or max
- `--session <id>` — named session slug for the selected engine; storage and resume compatibility are engine-specific
- `--continue` — continue a prior session using the selected engine's supported continuation semantics
- `--agent <name>` — agent template to use (V1 default: coder; opencode2 beta uses its built-in primary agent unless set)
- `--provider <name>` — canonical provider for this one run
- `--model <model>` — override the main model for this one run: <canonical-provider>/<native-id> selector, or a bare native id resolved against --provider or the effective default provider
- `--isolate` — run in a disposable git worktree under .triss/wt/<slug>
- `--no-isolate` — disable worktree isolation (opencode defaults to OFF; crush defaults to ON)
- `--restrict` — crush only: enforce the allowlist via CLI --allow-bash/--allow-tool flags (--restrict-run). Opt-in (default OFF)
- `--no-restrict` — crush only: disable restrict (crush auto-approves every tool — the default)
- `--cwd <path>` — working directory (ignored with --isolate)
- `--timeout <sec>` — kill the engine after this many seconds
- `--allow-best-effort-caller-worktree` — allow downgrade to caller worktree when isolated isolation cannot be enforced (default off — fails before spawn without it)
- `--protect-credentials` — Use the parent-owned credential proxy and strict executable-surface gates.
A selected protected route fails closed — before any credential-bearing
spawn — when the raw key cannot be contained or the proxy cannot start;
there is no automatic downgrade to raw. An explicit --no-protect-credentials
overrides a persisted TRISS_*_PROTECT_CREDENTIALS=true choice for this run.
- `--no-protect-credentials` — override a persisted TRISS_PROTECT_CREDENTIALS=true choice for this run
- `--stdin` — read the prompt from piped stdin instead of the [prompt] argument
- `--json` — no-op — the envelope is always JSON; kept for symmetry with other commands

## `triss coder clean`

Remove finished .triss/wt isolation worktrees (branches with no diff vs the default branch)

Options:

- `--all` — force-remove every worktree under .triss/wt, regardless of diff state

## `triss coder state`

Back up or validate the v2 coder state of a project (rollback contract)

## `triss coder state backup`

Create a bounded rollback backup of the v2 coder state (both engine session stores + coder-state-v2)

Options:

- `--project <absolute-path>` — absolute path of the validated project root
- `--backup <path>` — backup destination directory (default: <project>/.triss/backups/<timestamp>)
- `--json` — print the stable machine-readable result (no secrets)

## `triss coder state validate`

Validate a rollback backup: manifest schema, completion marker hash, per-entry verification

Options:

- `--project <absolute-path>` — absolute path of the validated project root
- `--backup <basename>` — backup directory to validate
- `--json` — print the stable machine-readable result (no secrets)

## `triss coder state adopt`

Adopt owned v2 state under a NEW project id: quarantine the old id, rewrite validated owner records

Options:

- `--from-project-id <32hex>` — the old project id (32 lowercase hex) to quarantine

## `triss coder state reset`

Quarantine all validated local v2 state and create an empty identity (never deletes it)

Options:

- `--project <absolute-path>` — absolute path of the validated project root

## `triss coder session`

List, clean, or migrate v2 isolated sessions (per-engine store; legacy .triss/sessions.json is never touched)

## `triss coder session list`

Serialize the bounded v2 session inventory projection to stdout

Options:

- `--engine <name>` — coding engine: opencode (default), opencode2, crush, or omp (see docs/engines/omp.md)

## `triss coder session clean`

Remove a selected inactive v2 isolated session/workspace transaction and its engine-owned store mapping (a row whose recorded owner provably died is reclaimed automatically; --recover-live attests a still-live-looking owner is gone)

Arguments:

- `<slug>`

Options:

- `--engine <name>` — coding engine: opencode, opencode2, crush, or omp (MANDATORY)
- `--recover-live` — force-clean a reserved/running session whose owner process may still appear live (you attest the owner is really gone)

## `triss coder session migrate`

One-shot upgrade of a released v0.39.0 (schema_version 1) engine inventory to the canonical schema: fully-idle documents gain freshly minted immutable session instance ids and the original document is preserved under .triss/quarantine-v1/. An inventory with any reserved/running/deleting legacy row fails closed without partial migration

Options:

- `--engine <name>` — coding engine: opencode, opencode2, crush, or omp (MANDATORY)

## `triss coder result`

List or clean retained result artifacts (never persistent sessions)

## `triss coder result list`

Serialize the bounded retained-result projection to stdout

## `triss coder result clean`

Remove only a validated retained result artifact (run-<32 lowercase hex>)

Arguments:

- `<run-id>`

## `triss mcp`

MCP server: register Triss as a tool provider for Claude Code and Codex

## `triss mcp serve`

Run the stdio MCP server. Claude Code starts this for you — no need to run it directly.

## `triss mcp install`

Register triss as MCP server for Claude Code (~/.claude.json) or Codex (~/.codex/config.toml)

Options:

- `-g, --global` — install into the agent global config (default)
- `-l, --local` — install into <cwd>/.mcp.json (claude only)
- `-t, --target <agent>` — target agent (claude | codex | both); omit for an interactive prompt
- `--command <cmd>` — override the executable name (default: triss)
- `--args <args>` — override args, space-separated (default: 'mcp serve')

## `triss mcp uninstall`

Remove the triss MCP entry from the config

Options:

- `-g, --global` — remove from the agent global config (default)
- `-l, --local` — remove from <cwd>/.mcp.json (claude only)
- `-t, --target <agent>` — target agent (claude | codex | both); omit for an interactive prompt

## `triss mcp status`

Show whether triss is registered and with what command

Options:

- `-g, --global` — (default) check the agent global config
- `-l, --local` — check <cwd>/.mcp.json (claude only)
- `-t, --target <agent>` — target agent (claude | codex | both). Default: both
